findings.title: The opening's directed exit
findings.claim: The focus's obstruction and wish for crookedness can be read against the opening movement out of darkness, into light, and toward a straight path: the obstruction interrupts a directed transition, not only access to a religious way.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb يَصُدُّونَ at 14:3:7:2 supplies turning away or holding back, while the opening verb at 14:1 word 5 and the path at word 14 supply a directed movement and destination. The darknesses and light in 14:1 complete that sequence. Contact with the focus's separate crookedness word at 14:3:12:1 makes the later obstruction legible as interference with the opening route's completion.
findings.reader_payoff: The path is perceived as a movement between states that can be interrupted, while the focus's ordinary claim about blocking God's way remains intact.
findings.containment: The focus still describes preference for worldly life, obstruction from God's way, and a desire to make it crooked. The 14:1 relation adds a transition image; the source itself leaves open whether the verses form one transport process or contrasting portraits. The focus leaves the blocked recipient unexpressed, so the transitive facet is retained as a bounded reading rather than a settled object analysis.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic anchors confirm the surface sequence and focus occurrences, but the context root, word-index, and branch links come from a legacy_unbound HFT trace. The contextual reading is retained with its live alternative visible.

findings.title: A dispute over the route's name
findings.claim: The focus's crookedness-seeking can be heard within a dispute over how the route is named: messengers clarify in their people's language, while rejecters describe that redirection as an attempt to turn them from their fathers' worship.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier عِوَجًا at 14:3:12:1 assigns a crooked quality to God's way. In 14:4, the messenger's own language and act of clarifying put guidance in a communicative field. In 14:10, rejecters use the same diversion root against the messengers and identify their fathers' worship as the route from which they fear being turned. These contacts reverse the charge of diversion and make the focus's pursuit of crookedness legible as a struggle over inherited route and its naming.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how calling a route crooked and calling a message a diversion become contested acts within the pericope.
findings.containment: The focus still says that the actors seek crookedness for God's way. The contextual material adds the rejecters' accusation and inherited worship as a competing frame; it does not establish that the messengers manipulate language or that the accusation settles which route is straight. A simpler local irony without broader semantic capture remains possible.

epistemic.reason: The supplied Arabic verifies the cited context surfaces, but the word coordinates and root-role links for 14:4 and 14:10 are attributed to a legacy_unbound HFT trace. The route-labeling claim is therefore qualified, with its simpler alternative preserved.

findings.title: Route control through land and belonging
findings.claim: The focus's obstruction and pursuit of crookedness take on a territorial force in the pericope: rejecters demand exile or return to their creed, while the answer promises settlement after them. The focus's pursuit can also resonate with overstepping and oppression in light of that ultimatum.
findings.mechanism: The focus's diversion verb at 14:3:7:2 meets an ultimatum in 14:13: expulsion from the land or return to the community's creed. The settlement promised at 14:14 reverses who occupies the land. That sequence gives route obstruction material instruments in residence and communal belonging. The focus's verb يَبْغُونَهَا at 14:3:11:2, whose ordinary construction is seeking crookedness, also contacts the overstepping facet of its root when placed beside the coercive ultimatum.
findings.reader_payoff: The route is seen as something whose passage, residence, and communal allegiance can be controlled, and the focus's seeking becomes perceptible alongside enacted pressure.
findings.containment: The focus still names preference, obstruction, and seeking crookedness. The later ultimatum adds a territorial instance and a bounded overreach resonance; it does not prove that every focus actor is identical with every speaker in the later scene or that the context exhausts the focus's meaning. The mountain-barrier branch is analogical: the focus uses a verb and does not name a mountain. The source's alternative that exile merely exemplifies hostility remains open.

epistemic.reason: The exact 14:13 and 14:14 Arabic confirms the ultimatum and settlement surfaces, but their word-index and root links are attributed to a legacy_unbound HFT trace. findings.title: The path under stated ownership
findings.claim: The focus's mention of Allah's path follows a statement of Allah's ownership of all in the heavens and earth and a warning to disbelievers, placing the actors' preference and obstruction within an explicit frame of divine ownership and consequence.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the proper name Allah in the phrase 'Allah's way' at 14:3:10:1. The preceding 14:2 states that all in the heavens and earth belong to Allah and warns disbelievers of severe punishment. The same named owner contacts the route the focus says is obstructed, so the choice of worldly life is seen against a pericope frame of ownership and warning.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the route's named owner and the warning before encountering the focus's description of preference and obstruction.
findings.containment: The focus supplies the preference and obstruction; 14:2 supplies a surrounding frame, not a proven individual motive. Its connection row is a nomination, and the target verse's morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: Both Arabic surfaces are supplied and the connection record names the ownership-and-warning relation, but 14:2 has no target morphology in the packet and the relation remains a contextual inference.
